affected_runtime_boundary: Python execution/import boundary feeding WP510 GWT causal-path subject freshness

do_not_merge_authorities.artifact_bound_static_completeness: Keep as release-artifact -> static-delivery composition only. Its own evidence scope excludes target runtime.
do_not_merge_authorities.wp510_runtime_subject_witness: Separate deterministic runtime-subject/freshness witness that may consume upstream release identity but cannot mint release/static/effect/completion authority.

best_supported_design_delta.name: WP510_RECURSIVE_RUNTIME_SUBJECT_WITNESS/v1
best_supported_design_delta.purpose: Permit bounded reuse of an already-measured WP510 semantic/runtime probe only when the exact relevant execution subject remains demonstrably unchanged; otherwise fail closed to REPROBE_REQUIRED.

required: sorted recursive local F2 dependency paths + per-file SHA-256
exact source/release generation identity when available
actual interpreter executable file SHA-256 + byte size
digest of actually consumed Python executable artifact when technically observable
explicit policy evidence excluding divergent cached/sourceless bytecode if consumed-byte attestation is unavailable
sorted locally loaded module identities/paths at the measured boundary
probe/result identity whose reuse is being requested

decision_states.REUSE_ELIGIBLE_RESEARCH_HYPOTHESIS: All required identities match, no dynamic hazard is unresolved, executed-artifact identity is bound or excluded by tested policy, and runtime-local module set remains within the sealed closure.
decision_states.REPROBE_REQUIRED_SOURCE_CHANGE: Root or any transitive local dependency identity changed.
decision_states.REPROBE_REQUIRED_DYNAMIC_SURFACE: Dynamic import, sys.path/meta/path-hook mutation, entry-point discovery, environment-dependent import behavior or native-loader surface is present without an admitted stronger witness.
decision_states.REPROBE_REQUIRED_RUNTIME_MISMATCH: Runtime local-module observation contains material not in the sealed static closure.
decision_states.REPROBE_REQUIRED_EXECUTED_ARTIFACT_UNPRO: Source/interpreter may match but actually consumed cached/sourceless bytecode or loader artifact is not proved equal/excluded.
decision_states.BLOCKED_PROVENANCE_AMBIGUOUS: Generation, release, source, probe, or witness subject cannot be bound exactly.

why_now: E3-v2 reproduced a seven-file WP510 local closure on exact source with no detected dynamic/external local closure gap and no runtime-extra local modules.
E4-v2 showed closure digest invalidation under transitive byte mutation and static dependency addition, and fail-closed behavior for dynamic import/sys.path/entry-point/environment/native hazards.
The repaired instrument proved interpreter executable byte identity separately from path identity.
Parallel Trigger-6 evidence shows .py source identity can diverge from executed .pyc identity, so an E5 candidate omitting consumed execution-artifact identity would overclaim freshness.

external_primary_support.claim: Python supports timestamp- and hash-based cached bytecode; unchecked hash pycs can be assumed valid by the import system subject to interpreter policy.
PEP 552 defines CHECKED_HASH/UNCHECKED_HASH behavior and --check-hash-based-pycs policy, establishing a concrete source-vs-cached-bytecode identity divergence surface.
Python exposes source, sourceless-bytecode, extension loaders, path finders/hooks and cached bytecode machinery; source-file path alone is not a complete execution-subject witness.
Distribution/entry-point discovery depends on import search machinery including sys.path/meta-path context, supporting fail-closed treatment of plugin discovery.

efficiency_design.steady_state: Do not recursively parse/hash source on every model request. Capture/seal at artifact/generation activation or first accepted measurement, cache the canonical witness digest, and compare bounded generation/subject identity on reuse attempts.
efficiency_design.expected_dependency_weight: stdlib-only implementation candidate; no external framework required
efficiency_design.expected_steady_state_overhead: near-O(1) digest/state comparison after sealed capture; must be measured by Trigger-4
efficiency_design.capture_cost: O(bytes of bounded recursive source closure + interpreter executable + observed execution artifacts); must be measured and cached

required_trigger4_tests: clean exact WP510 subject -> candidate witness can be captured but grants no E6 by itself
unrelated repository file mutation -> sealed WP510 closure identity remains stable
transitive WP510 source byte mutation with unchanged root -> REPROBE_REQUIRED_SOURCE_CHANGE
dynamic import to an extra local module -> REPROBE_REQUIRED_DYNAMIC_SURFACE and/or RUNTIME_MISMATCH
entry-point/plugin discovery -> REPROBE_REQUIRED_DYNAMIC_SURFACE unless stronger admitted plugin inventory witness exists
unchecked-hash stale pyc fixture -> source equality must not produce REUSE unless consumed pyc identity is bound or policy forces source validation
sourceless pyc fixture -> fail closed or bind exact consumed bytecode subject
runtime local-module set outside static closure -> REPROBE_REQUIRED_RUNTIME_MISMATCH
required_measurements: bytes hashed and files opened per capture/recompute
false-reuse count across adversarial fixtures (must be zero)
counterhypotheses: WP510 bounded probe replay is so cheap that witness capture/maintenance has worse total cost than simply reprobe.
Exact F2 execution launcher already excludes divergent pyc/plugin/import-environment behavior and receipts that invariant, making part of this witness redundant.
Python execution subject is too dynamic for a safe closed witness; in that case retain REPROBE_REQUIRED rather than weakening the gate.
rollback_or_reject: Reject or reduce the witness if Trigger-4 shows no measurable saved probe cost, unacceptable false invalidation, any false reuse, or overlap with an already stronger admitted execution-subject authority.
